{"m": "gpt-4o", "msg": [{"content": "You compare short personal anecdotes by their underlying relational structure - the pattern of intentions, causes, deceptions, reversals, and outcomes among the people involved - NOT by their surface topic, setting, or vocabulary. Two stories can be about totally different situations yet share the same deep structure; two stories can share the same topic yet have opposite structure.", "role": "system"}, {"content": "SITUATION:
When I was up for promotion, my friendly colleague Mark said he'd put in a good word for me. My openly competitive colleague Janet, who I assumed wanted me to fail, quietly sent the committee examples of my best work. I got promoted. Mark had actually told them I wasn't ready.

CANDIDATE A:
My mother-in-law, who I thought disapproved of me, secretly told my husband to fight for our marriage during our rough patch. My best friend, who was 'always there for me,' had been encouraging him to leave. Mom saved my marriage; my friend almost destroyed it.

CANDIDATE B:
When I was up for promotion, my friendly colleague Mark said he'd put in a good word for me—and he did, praising my work to the committee. My competitive colleague Janet, predictably, said nothing supportive. Mark's advocacy helped, and I got promoted. The colleague who seemed supportive was supportive; the one who seemed competitive stayed competitive. People were exactly as they appeared.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:10"}
content: {"choice": "A", "reason": "Both stories involve a reversal of expectations where the seemingly supportive person undermines and the seemingly competitive or disapproving person actually helps."}
